NICE says about half of the estimated 635,000 people in England with heart failure have preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction.
NICE has published final draft guidance that recommends finerenone for adults with chronic heart failure that has preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction.
Finerenone belongs to a group of medicines called mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.
NICE estimates that up to 280,000 people could be eligible for it.
NICE says that of the estimated 635,000 people in England who have heart failure, about half have preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction.
The announcement also reports around 100,000 hospital admissions for heart failure in England in 2023 to 2024.
NICE recommended dapagliflozin in 2023 for the same group of people, and it was the first NICE-recommended treatment for this type of heart failure.
Final draft guidance is the stage before NICE publishes its final guidance.
